mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate above 5.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that compresses equity valuations by increasing discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (as of t-1mo), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5 and rising > 0.3pp over 3 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in the past month signals a contraction in consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < -1% and RSAFS < -1% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by >1% in the past month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime (INDPRO < 110.0), a further decline in industrial production by more than 0.5% in the past month signals worsening supply conditions that increase input costs and reduce corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 110.0 and INDPRO decline > 0.5% in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0 and INDPRO decline > 0.5% in the past month, or the Rank IC for the INDPRO decline in the supply shock regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained high level of housing starts (HOUST > 1400 thousand units) signals strong consumer demand and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1400, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A 12-month increase in the CPI above 2.5% signals rising inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rise > 2.5% over 12 months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% and 0.3pp respectively in the past month signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in the past month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS decline > 0.5% and UNRATE rise > 0.3pp in the past month, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%), a further increase in the federal funds rate signals continued restrictive policy that dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS increases in the past month, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
